payload.feature:
Decision 0040 is accepted (ruled 2026-09-04; docs/decisions/0040-the-flag-is-always-read.md). Enact it. Read the decision first: each of its five rulings names an enforcement binding, and those bindings are this commission — nothing beyond them. Also read the notes on PRs #160 and #161, where the five findings this decision closes were recorded by the reviewers.

1. `--model` is always read (ruling 1). In crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs, `enforce_model_policy` reads an inline site's route pin on the adapter's declared `model_flag` AND on `--model`. Same string: one read, as today. Different strings: a concrete pin on either names the route; two concrete pins naming different ids are Unreadable and refused naming both flags; an adapter declaring `model_flag: "unsupported"` still has `--model` read and a pin found there is Unreadable (a provider that cannot be told a model has no route to name), never the adapter's own class. Tests in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/model_policy_tests.rs: a `-m` adapter with egress contracted and a secret-binding seat writing `--model elsewhere/large-1` is refused (red before the fix); `-m a/x --model b/y` refused naming both flags; `model_flag: "unsupported"` with `--model spark/x` refused; `-m spark/x` alone on a `spark: local` route still binds. `model_pin` and `command_pins_effort` (decisions 0031 and 0035) do not change.

2. A spelling is decided by the flag's shape (ruling 2). Replace `UnreadSpelling` in `command_pin` with a reading derived from the flag string: a LONG flag (two dashes) has exactly `FLAG VALUE` and `FLAG=VALUE`, and any other word beginning with it is a different flag walked past by every reader; a SHORT flag (one dash, one character) has those two plus the attached `FLAGVALUE`, read as a pin whose value is the remainder, and a remainder that is not one concrete model id is Unreadable. Tests: the long neighbour (`--model-fallback`) walked past on both the 0031 reader and the 0036 reader; `-mspark/x` read as a route; `-march=native` under `-m` refused on a secret-binding seat.

3. A refusal names the flags it read (ruling 3). Remove the `unwrap_or("--model")` fallback in the Unreadable refusal; the message names the declared flag, `--model`, or both, exactly as the read used them; asserted in the tests above.

4. Ambient means unbound by any seat (ruling 4). In crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs, `report_ambient_credentials` takes the inspected bundle's declared secret names (every seat's `secrets`, through the composed bundle): a route's credential is ambient when the process environment holds the variable and no seat declares it, whatever the store holds. Without a bundle to inspect, doctor reports store membership and says that is what it checked. Tests in crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor/tests.rs: held-and-declared is silent; held-and-undeclared with the variable exported warns by route; the no-bundle wording.

5. A route name is whatever a model id may begin with (ruling 5). In crates/brokkr-runtime/src/agents/load.rs add a `ROUTE_GRAMMAR` constant — ASCII letters of either case, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`, `:`; never `/` — used for the keys of both `routes` and `credentials` and quoted in their refusals; the agent-name grammar stays for agents, adapters and abstract model names. Tests in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/agents/tests.rs: `us.east` and `openai_compat` declared and each resolved through a prefixed pin; a key containing `/` refused.

Do not touch: any adapter JSON, the wire protocol, any journal row, the tier vocabulary, decision 0021's rulings, or the witness digests — no adapter data changes, so no bundle digest should move; if one does, name why in the commit. Full gate as the verify seat knows it, exact coverage included; every new refusal has a test that trips it.

No adapter JSON, wire protocol, journal rows, tier vocabulary, decision 0021, or witness digests are to be touched; no bundle digest should move. Coherent, no frozen-contract conflict.

Decision 0040 enacted, one binding per ruling and nothing beyond them. (1) enforce_model_policy now reads an inline site's route on the adapter's declared model_flag AND on --model: same string is one read; different strings join per the ruling — a concrete pin on either names the route, two pins naming different ids are Unreadable refused naming both flags; model_flag: "unsupported" still has --model read and a pin there is Unreadable, never the adapter's class. The reviewer's fail-open scenario (-m adapter, egress contracted, secret-binding seat writing --model elsewhere/large-1) was an `expect(compile)` before and is a refusal assertion now, so the red is visible in the diff. model_pin (0031) and command_pins_effort (0035) unchanged. (2) UnreadSpelling removed; command_pin derives the spelling from the flag string via short_flag() — long flag has FLAG VALUE and FLAG=VALUE only and any longer word is a neighbour both readers walk past; short flag adds the attached FLAGVALUE read as a pin whose value is the remainder, Unreadable when the remainder is not one concrete id. (3) unwrap_or("--model") removed; ModelPin::Unreadable carries the flags the read used and unreadable_destination() names them ('-m', '--model', or both), asserted in the tests. (4) report_ambient_credentials takes the inspected bundle's declared secret names (union of every seat's secrets); doctor compiles the bundle before the ambient report and reports it after, so the bundle line keeps its place; with no bundle (or one that does not compile) it reports store membership and says so in the line. (5) ROUTE_GRAMMAR ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$ added in agents/load.rs, keys both routes and credentials, quoted in both refusals; NAME_GRAMMAR untouched. Tests: every case each enforcement binding names, plus the empty and '/'-bearing route keys and a direct unit test of short_flag's shapes. Three existing tests that asserted the superseded behaviour were rewritten. No adapter JSON, wire protocol, journal row or tier vocabulary touched; witness_digests and every other suite green, so no digest moved. Gate run locally: cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked, clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, compile of bundles/self and bundles/verify, and exact coverage via cargo +nightly llvm-cov (lines 16140/16140, branches 2458/2458, functions 1531/1531 — one branch was red on the first pass, a double-pin through two attached spellings, and is now covered). Also corrected the doctor sentence in docs/guides/provider-adapters.md, which stated the superseded store-membership rule, and added the flag and route grammars beside it. Committed signed as 62b1de8 on slice-flag-enact; not pushed.

RESIDUAL 1 — low, security-adjacent (credential visibility). crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs:140-146. With a bundle inspected, `covered` is `declared.contains(variable)` alone; store membership is dropped entirely. So a credential that IS declared by some seat, is NOT in the bindings store, and IS exported in the environment is now silent, where the old store-membership reading warned. Proved with a probe: store empty, one seat declaring NEARBY_API_KEY, ambient true -> "route nearby" is not reported. The declaring seat does hard-refuse at spawn (secret::resolve_bindings errors on a name the store lacks), which closes most of it — but `declared` is a UNION over all seats, so a sibling seat on the same route that does NOT declare the name still spawns and its driver reads the launching shell's copy, unreported. This matches ruling 4's operative clause literally ("no seat ... declares it"), but it drops the same ruling's next clause, "store membership is necessary for a binding but is not one" — necessary was not enforced. The fix is a one-line conjunction plus a test, but it narrows a frozen ruling's semantics, so it is the operator's call and not a reviewer's small safe fix. Left unfixed and recorded.

RESIDUAL 2 — info, wording. doctor.rs:291-303 with tests.rs asserting it: a bundle that was GIVEN but fails to compile emits "no bundle was inspected". Defensible (the code comment argues an untrusted compile is no bundle to inspect) and deliberately pinned by a test, but an operator who passed --bundle and sees "MISSING bundle" alongside "no bundle was inspected" reads a contradiction. Cosmetic.

OBSERVATION — info, not a finding. Ruling 2's short-attached reading means any word beginning with a declared short flag whose remainder is id-shaped is now a pin: '-max' under '-m' reads as pin "ax", which has no '/', resolves unprefixed, and hands the site the adapter's OWN class — where before the ruling it was Unreadable and fell to the uncontracted floor. Verified by probe (compiles on a contracted adapter). This is the ruled grammar applied uniformly (every unprefixed concrete pin rides the adapter's own class), and ruling 2 names only the non-id remainder ('-march=native', which carries '=') as the refusal case. Recorded so the shift from fail-closed to adapter-class on this shape is on the record rather than discovered later.

No security finding at high or critical: nothing touches seat-result or driver-output parsing, the journal, the wire protocol or secret VALUES. Refusal text and doctor lines carry flag strings, route names and variable names only — never a value; the ambient probe is still a boolean. Correctness and simplicity are otherwise clean: UnreadSpelling is gone rather than left dead, the caller-supplied parameter is removed from all three call sites, model_pin and command_pins_effort keep 0031's and 0035's question unchanged (both read long flags, which walk past neighbours exactly as before), and the unwrap_or("--model") fallback is gone with tests asserting no constant stands in (!refusal.contains("unsupported'"), !refusal.contains("'-m' and")).

Commit 639c67a, three files: doctor.rs, doctor/tests.rs, docs/guides/provider-adapters.md.

RESIDUAL 1 (low, security-adjacent) closed. doctor.rs computed `covered` as `declared.contains(variable)` alone, which enacted ruling 4's first clause and dropped its second — 'store membership is necessary for a binding but is not one'. I read enforcing the necessity as enactment rather than amendment: the ruling states it in the same sentence, and dropping it reopens the exact false negative ruling 4 exists to close. A name a seat DECLARES that the store cannot answer for is bound to nothing; the declaring seat refuses at spawn, but `declared` is a union over all seats, so a sibling seat on the same route that does not declare the name spawns anyway and its driver reads the launching shell's copy, unreported. `covered` is now `declared.contains(variable) && in_store(variable)`, and the warning names which half failed instead of borrowing the other's reason. This only ADDS warnings, and only where the store cannot bind anything — no case warns wrongly.

Red-before-fix proved in my own hands: reverting just the conjunction fails the new test `doctor_reads_a_declared_name_the_store_cannot_answer_for_as_ambient` and leaves the other twelve doctor tests green, so the new test is precisely what pins the new reading. Restored and re-run green.

RESIDUAL 2 (info, wording) closed with it. `declared: Option<_>` was None both for 'no bundle passed' and 'bundle passed did not compile', so an operator reading `MISSING bundle` was told two lines later they had inspected no bundle. A `Seats` enum (Declared / NoBundleGiven / BundleDidNotCompile) makes the tri-state explicit; each says which silence it is. Deliberately NO derive on it — a `Clone` nobody calls is a function the exact-coverage gate counts and no test can reach; it is passed and matched by reference instead.

The reviewer's OBSERVATION (short attached `-max` reading as pin 'ax' and riding the adapter's own class) I left alone: it is ruling 2's grammar applied uniformly, every unprefixed concrete pin rides the adapter's own class, and ruling 2 names only the non-id remainder (`-march=native`) as the refusal case. Changing it would be legislating past the ruling.

CORRECTNESS — all five bindings land, and each new refusal has a test that trips it. Ruling 1: inline_route_pin (bundle.rs:470) joins route_pin on the declared model_flag and on --model, filtering the declared read out when the two strings coincide (so the shipped five, all --model, keep exactly one read). SIMPLICITY — no dead policy and no overbuild. UnreadSpelling and its caller-supplied parameter are removed rather than left beside the new reading; ModelPin::Unreadable now carries the flags instead of a constant being reconstructed at the refusal; Seats deliberately derives no Clone (a derived-and-uncalled impl is a function the exact-coverage gate counts). The doctor compile is hoisted and REUSED — the bundle is compiled once, not twice — and the bundle report line stays last where the operator reads it. I walked every new arm for the exact-coverage gate and found each one reachable from a test, including both unreadable_destination arities, all three Seats variants, both Declared sub-arms, and route_name's empty case; I did not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh here because it exports CARGO_LLVM_COV_TARGET_DIR into a mktemp under /tmp, which on this host is a 31G tmpfs that a workspace-wide instrumented build has previously filled. Note that the verify seat's typed result also carried no coverage input — CI's 'exact coverage gate' job is the remaining unrun piece of the full gate.

SECURITY — one residual, LOW, and it is the ruling's own boundary rather than a deviation from it.

1. [low, security] doctor's ambient report reads seat declarations as a UNION over the whole bundle, so a bundle where one seat declares a credential and a sibling seat on the same route does not is silent about the sibling. crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs:180 — Seats::Declared(declared) => declared.contains(variable) && in_store(variable). The new test fixture is itself an instance: bundle_binding() builds seat 'work' with secrets and seat 'review' with none, both dispatching driver 'many' on route nearby, and doctor_reads_ambient_against_the_bundles_own_bindings_not_the_store asserts route nearby is silent when the store holds NEARBY_API_KEY and 'work' declares it. At run time seat 'review' spawns with nothing bound and its driver reads the launching shell's copy of NEARBY_API_KEY — a value journaled nowhere and moving no digest, on exactly the channel 0036 ruling 5 and 0040 ruling 4 exist to make visible. NOT fixed, and I judge it should not be fixed here: ruling 4's own words are "NO seat of the inspected bundle declares it in secrets", which IS the union, and the commission is the five bindings and nothing beyond them. Per-seat reporting is a new question for a new decision. The implementer names this residual in the doc comment at doctor.rs:135 and reaches for store membership as a partial cover, but the store half does not close it: the case above has both halves satisfied and stays silent. Severity low because doctor is advisory and gates nothing, the ambient channel is permitted by design, and the shape requires the operator's own bundle to bind a name unevenly across seats.

Considered and rejected as findings: (a) a declared flag of one dash and two-plus characters (-mo) is read with the two long spellings, so a getopt-attached value on it would be walked past — but ruling 2 defines short as exactly one dash and one character, and no real convention gives -moVALUE that meaning (Go-style single-dash flags do not take attached values either), so the code is faithful and the gap is not reachable; (b) reading --model on an adapter that does not honour it can now promote a site to a declared-local route on a word the provider ignores — explicitly ruled by 0040's closing paragraph ("a pin the provider ignores is still a pin the operator wrote"); (c) long neighbours now walking past on the route reader is a widening over #161 — that IS ruling 2; (d) ROUTE_GRAMMAR admitting a leading '-' or '.' — route names are never used as paths or argv words, only as map keys and report text; (e) pub on ROUTE_GRAMMAR reaching nobody outside the private load module — matches SECRET_NAME_GRAMMAR's existing idiom in the same file. No secret VALUE is read or printed anywhere in the new code: store_names returns names, secrets is a list of names, and the ambient probe returns a bool.

Third implement visit, entered on REVIEW-REFORGE carrying the review's one surviving residual (low, security): doctor's ambient report reads seat declarations as a UNION over the whole bundle, so a bundle where one seat declares a credential and a sibling seat on the same route does not is silent about the sibling, whose driver then reads the launching shell's copy. I answered the finding and made NO code change, because the fix it asks for is outside the commission. Nothing is committed this visit; HEAD is unchanged at 639c67a and the tree is clean.

WHY THE RESIDUAL IS NOT FIXED HERE. Ruling 4's own words are the union: 'reports a route's credential as ambient when the process environment holds the variable and NO seat of the inspected bundle declares it in secrets'. Reporting the sibling means inverting that quantifier — warn when SOME seat does not declare it — which is an amendment to the ruling, not its enactment. The previous visit's added conjunct (store membership is necessary) was different in kind: the ruling states it in the same sentence, so enforcing it was reading the whole sentence. There is no such sentence for the sibling case. It is also not a one-line inversion in practice: report_ambient_credentials walks the ADAPTERS' credentials by route and knows nothing about which seats resolve to which route, so a per-seat reading as the code stands would warn on every route whose credential is not declared by every seat, including seats that never touch that provider.
